title: Independent review of remaining round-1 DOM benchmark results
reviewType: Saved results/evidence audit, not a code review or new acquisition
verdictDefinition: QUALIFIED WITH LIMITS preserves the measured direction and ratio as a local instrumented whole-terminal observation. It does not qualify a general equal-raster or isolated-renderer efficiency headline.

unicode-emoji.verdictSummary: Two-pair instrumented default-surface observation; unequal width/scrollbar and Unicode composition; no equal-raster or isolated-renderer claim.
unicode-emoji.qualifiedClaim: A lower-in-both-pairs saved instrumented whole-terminal CPU/instruction/estimated-CPU-energy observation on the default R06 Unicode surfaces.
limits: Default surfaces differ: native inferred grid 280x228 CSS px versus recorded xterm grid 288x228 CSS px, with an xterm scrollbar thumb. Actual visible native DIV bounds were not recorded for R06.

Mode 2027 is off, but the same retained Unicode strings produce visibly different woman-technologist ZWJ composition. This qualifies a default-surface/text-equivalent observation only; strict equal-raster Unicode work is not qualified.

Two balanced adjacent pairs in one session are a descriptive result for this workload, host and sealed bundle. No significance, confidence interval, cross-session repeatability or broad renderer-efficiency claim is established.

The research observer is enabled for both arms but its overhead is uncalibrated and its wrapped internal methods differ. This is an instrumented whole-terminal comparison, not an overhead-corrected isolated DOM-renderer comparison.

Coverage is the stable CDP-enumerated endpoint PID/type/start family. Entirely transient processes are unobservable; sequential CDP and per-PID native samples are non-atomic and have different boundaries.

The endpoint demonstrates logical settlement after the common reset, paced writes and two RAFs. It does not demonstrate physical presentation or zero delayed browser/compositor/device work after the endpoint.

The sealed older reader has validated ABI/units and positive observed aggregate channels, but these runs carry no owned-helper startup capability-calibration metadata. Later collector calibration/enclosure cannot be retroactively attributed to this acquisition.
Energy is the kernel estimate of process CPU energy; GPU-process CPU work is included as a process channel, while GPU-device, display, non-Chrome and whole-device energy are outside scope.
Text equality trims trailing whitespace per row and checks retained strings, not exact glyph pixels or hidden-history style attributes.

method.comparison: ghostty DomTerminalRenderer versus xterm 6.0.0 stock DOM
method.ratioDirection: ghostty DOM numerator / xterm DOM denominator in both pairs
method.summary: Median of the two per-pair ratios; for n=2 this is their arithmetic midpoint. No pooling of totals or pair reassignment.
method.independentRecomputation: Python exact-integer subtraction of saved decimal-string per-process cumulative native counters; independent CDP cpuTime subtraction; fresh aggregation and ratio/median calculation before comparison to lane evaluation.
method.nativeCpuSeconds: (delta ri_user_time + delta ri_system_time) / 1e9; saved reader uses integer Mach-to-ns conversion with timebase 125/3
method.cdpCpuSeconds: delta SystemInfo.getProcessInfo cpuTime, reported separately from native CPU
method.instructions: delta ri_instructions; total across P and E core classes
method.cycles: delta ri_cycles; total across P and E core classes
method.estimatedCpuEnergyJ: delta ri_energy_nj / 1e9; kernel process CPU-energy estimate
method.effectiveClockGHz: cycles / matching native CPU seconds / 1e9; diagnostic average counter ratio, not a frequency trace
method.pCoreTimeShare: (delta ri_user_ptime + delta ri_system_ptime) / (delta ri_user_time + delta ri_system_time)

channels.renderer: All CDP type=renderer processes, including idle renderers
channels.GPU: CDP GPU process CPU work; not GPU-device work
channels.rendererPlusGPU: Union of renderer and GPU process groups

method.textBoundary: Full retained strings and SHA-256 after common trailing-whitespace normalization; visible strings, row count and head/tail independently checked. No hidden-history-style or glyph-pixel oracle.
method.endBoundary: Reset + paced public byte writes + two RAFs + observer snapshots, followed by sequential CDP/native snapshot. Full text readback, direct geometry and PNG capture are later, outside native counter windows.
method.observerScope: Uncalibrated research observer for both arms; native and xterm internal wrapper counts differ.
method.screenshots: Original PNGs hash-verified against raw index and output archive. Reviewer first-host crops use saved section bounds at DPR 2 without resampling; paired image adds labels only. Crops are later-readback evidence, not endpoint completion proof.

2_equal_public_work_implementations_geom.outcome: PASS public work, DOM selection and normalized line/edits geometry; Unicode surface/composition limited

3_counters_host_guards_turns_custody.outcome: PASS saved endpoint/sample/custody checks; non-atomic, endpoint-only and older-reader limits retained

findings.finding: All five saved metrics, all five process channels, both adjacent-pair directions and all medians independently reproduce. Pair 1 is DOM[0]/XDOM[1]; pair 2 is DOM[3]/XDOM[2]. The median of two ratios is their arithmetic midpoint, not a ratio of pooled totals.
findings.detail: Native CPU/instruction/energy medians reproduce the reported six decimals. Edits native CPU rounds to 1.069408; independently computed CDP CPU rounds to 1.069410. Unicode and line-scroll are lower in both pairs; edits has higher CPU, instructions and CPU-energy in both pairs, while cycles are lower.

findings.finding: The 12 windows each retain 17 actual DOM targets, 120 warmup ticks and 900 paid ticks, equal public byte writes, equal 40x12 logical grids and DPR 2. The native implementation is DomTerminalRenderer; xterm is 6.0.0 stock DOM, with no loaded WebGL renderer or xterm canvas surface.
findings.detail: Each paid target performs 901 public writes including a 19-byte reset. Independent expected-text reconstruction matches all 204 target readbacks, full retained-text digests and history counts. Native core writes, updates, acknowledgements and publications complete; xterm parser/write callbacks complete. Native transparent canvas is a geometry anchor beside the visible DIV, not a rendering fallback. Common retention cap is 200000 rows, native byte budget 67108864; these fixtures retain only 901 or 12 rows.

findings.finding: Normalized line-scroll and edits have directly observed 360x288 CSS px visible DIV grids, 360x288 client boxes, 24px row height, 15px Bench Mono, all 17 targets on-screen, before and after all four windows per workload.
findings.detail: All 272 before/after target observations pass. The native scrollbar and both xterm tracks have display:none, zero-sized rects and false visibility. Direct readback records the actual DOM text surface, rather than inferring visibility from the transparent native canvas. This normalizes visible extent, not the internal amount of terminal work.

evidence.location: 1-41: visible grid observer; 44-51: common panel and scrollbar CSS

findings.finding: Unicode R06 is text-equivalent but not equal-raster work. Native nominal grid is 280x228 CSS px inferred from the 560x456 transparent anchor at DPR 2; xterm reports 288x228 CSS px. Saved screenshots show an xterm scrollbar thumb and different ZWJ glyph composition.
findings.detail: The same woman-technologist sequence is retained on both sides, but the native screenshot shows separate woman/laptop glyphs while xterm composes a joined glyph. Common mode-2027-off input does not establish equal browser shaping. R06 lacks direct native visible-DIV measurements. The roughly 2.8% width difference cannot be used to numerically correct the measured ratio, and there is no evidence that subtracting scrollbar/shaping cost would preserve its magnitude. The default-surface observation can be stated with these limits; an equal-raster Unicode renderer-efficiency headline cannot.

findings.finding: All 24 endpoint samples cover the same seven CDP PID/type/start identities within each window, with native coverage, positive start identity, zero exit identity, monotone counters and ordered per-PID acquisition. No recorded Mac turn overlaps the three dataset turns; all admissions and cleanup receipts pass.
findings.detail: There are 84 paired per-process deltas. Each window enumerates browser, three renderer processes, GPU, network service and storage service. Every dataset records 17 owned PIDs dead, empty remaining-owned-process search and controller exit 0 under 590 seconds. AC/load admission and visible/focused display checks pass. These are saved endpoint/sample/custody facts, not continuous OS-wide isolation, load, power or process-lifecycle coverage.

findings.finding: The old collector executes CDP then native at both endpoints. The samples are sequential and non-atomic; native counters do not enclose the CDP interval as the newer collector does. Python monotonic and Node hrtime have distinct origins here.
findings.detail: Durations are computed only within each clock domain. Across the saved endpoints the largest full Node snapshot envelope is 2.229625ms and the largest Python native-read duration is 0.225833ms. These are observed acquisition diagnostics, not an error bound on performance ratios or proof that all delayed work is included. A cross-runtime absolute timestamp subtraction is invalid and is not used. Startup capability metadata is absent in the sealed R06 reader; the ABI/units validation and separately saved later capability calibration do not change these raw acquisitions.

evidence.location: 8-33: ABI and integer time conversion; 45-60: Python timestamps and ready metadata

findings.finding: Unequal auxiliary/internal work remains possible and partly observed. Cursor blink and accessibility are off, the cursor is hidden, but scrollbar management, link machinery, retained-history processing, frame publication and observer callbacks are not isolated away.
findings.detail: Native wraps six internal method boundaries and xterm wraps two, in addition to common public-write accounting; no DOM observer ON/OFF calibration was acquired. Native shows 901 renderer callbacks per target; xterm shows 1791 in Unicode/line-scroll and 901 in edits. LayoutCount deltas are 15317 in every native window versus xterm 983 Unicode, 911 line-scroll and 901 edits. Native painted-row deltas are 10702 per Unicode/line-scroll target and 913 per edits target; no matched xterm painted-row counter is available. These are architecture-specific counters, not equal-work gates or causal attribution. Native source constructs only the visible 12 DOM rows, so retained-history equality is not proof of equal offscreen processing. No fixture contains a URL and native endpoint diagnostics report no pending link resolution, but no paired link-layer execution/DOM inventory or post-endpoint work trace proves equal ancillary cost.

evidence.location: 57: accessibility flag; 122/147: native blink/accessibility; 236-237: xterm options; 292: cursor hide

findings.finding: Two pairs support the observed same-session directions, not statistical significance or reproducibility. The 17 terminals share a measured browser/process family and are not 17 independent samples; the 900 ticks and per-PID rows also are not independent replications.
findings.detail: Balanced A/B/B/A mitigates simple order drift but cannot bound systematic observer, shaping, ancillary-work, host-load or acquisition-boundary effects. No confidence interval or generalized probability of winning is justified. No candidate KEEP decision follows from these counterpart baselines. Edits instruction/CPU-energy loss is not explained away by its lower cycles or by a CPU-only clock effect; attribution remains open.

evidence.location: datasets.*.pairs; window channels and effective clocks

findings.finding: All three protocols were registered before driver start and acquisition. The four original rows are retained in order, the embedded protocol matches its stage hash, and sealed input/output artifacts match. No reviewed window was dropped, rescored or replaced in the retained evidence.
findings.detail: Earlier R01/R02/R05 registrations for these remaining workloads were abandoned before acquisition. Only the still-unacquired line-scroll/edits R06 protocols were prospectively superseded by normalized R06g; completed Unicode R06 was not repeated. Failed rolling trace attempts and a later edits BASE/CANDIDATE experiment remain separate and are not used as replacements. The local artifact and turn-log inventory cannot prove the absence of an unrecorded acquisition outside that record, and registration timestamps are saved records rather than independent trusted timestamp attestations.
